title: Knowledge check: Response Lifecycle and Common Mistakes

questions.prompt: In Response Lifecycle and Common Mistakes, which statement best describes Sending a response exactly once?
options: Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.

Connect this syllabus point to Response Lifecycle and Common Mistakes: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
Normalize expected failures into safe, predictable responses and forward unexpected failures to the final error handler. Keep diagnostic details in protected logs, not public responses.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Response Lifecycle and Common Mistakes?
options: Treat req as untrusted request context and res as a one-way response lifecycle. Choose content type, status, headers, and file/cookie behavior deliberately, and finish each branch without sending twice.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

questions.prompt: A change related to Response Lifecycle and Common Mistakes appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
